gloss: scrap of paper; slip of paper

definitions.gloss: scrap of paper; slip of paper
definitions.explanation: A small or insignificant piece of paper. Can be neutral (a memo or note) or dismissive (implying something is worthless).

examples.english: I jotted it down on a scrap of paper.

examples.japanese: ポケットから{紙切|かみき}れが{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: A slip of paper came out of my pocket.

examples.japanese: こんな{契約書|けいやくしょ}はただの{紙切|かみき}れにすぎない。
examples.english: A contract like this is nothing more than a worthless piece of paper.

notes:
Composed of {紙|かみ} (paper) + {切|き}れ (piece, scrap). The suffix 〜{切|き}れ indicates a small fragment cut or torn from something larger.

When used literally, it simply means a small piece of paper. When used figuratively — especially with ただの{紙切|かみき}れ — it dismisses something (a document, certificate, or contract) as worthless or meaningless.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ただの{紙切|かみき}れ: just a scrap of paper (dismissive)
- {一枚|いちまい}の{紙切|かみき}れ: a single piece of paper
- {紙切|かみき}れにすぎない: nothing more than a piece of paper

RELATED WORDS:
- {布切|ぬのき}れ: scrap of cloth — same pattern with fabric
- {端切|はぎ}れ: remnant, scrap — leftover fabric from cutting
